opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing new data-infrastructure chips and platforms; up 28% YoY, including teams from the Celestial AI and XConn acquisitions.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling the chips and running the company; up 39% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring related charges (gains), net
opex.note: Restructuring charges this quarter — severance and facility-exit costs, net of gains — versus a net gain a year ago.

follow100Note: Marvell kept only $1.43 of every $100 this quarter — a $331.8M paper charge on the Celestial AI deal price, plus heavy stock pay and acquisition amortization, ate most of the operating profit.
footerNote: Marvell guided Q2 FY27 revenue to $2.7B ±5% and raised its FY27 and FY28 revenue outlook on AI bookings.
oneTimers: Inside the $203.3M other expense, net: the fair value of the contingent consideration owed for Celestial AI rose $331.8M — a non-cash charge — partly offset by an $81.1M unrealized gain on a forward stock purchase contract. Both are excluded from non-GAAP results.

GAAP profit is far below non-GAAP profit ($34.5M vs $718.0M) mainly because GAAP includes $207.6M of stock-based compensation and $225.2M of amortization of acquired intangible assets, both excluded from non-GAAP.
Marvell closed two acquisitions in the quarter — Celestial AI on February 2, 2026 and XConn on February 10, 2026 — and their results are included from those dates.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $52.8M plus other expense, net of $203.3M — a net $256.1M non-operating loss. Inside it, a $331.8M rise in the fair value of the Celestial acquisition contingent consideration was partly offset by an $81.1M gain on a forward stock purchase contract.

segments.name: Data center
segments.note: Chips for AI data centers — custom silicon, 800G/1.6T optics and Ethernet switches; a record quarter, 76% of all revenue.

segments.name: Communications and other
segments.note: Carrier, enterprise networking, automotive and industrial markets.

takeaways.text: Data Center revenue hit a record $1.83B — 76% of the company — on AI demand for custom XPU silicon, optics and scale-out switches.
takeaways.title: Data Center set the record

takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was just 4 cents against 80 cents non-GAAP: a $331.8M Celestial deal fair-value charge, $207.6M of stock pay and $225.2M of acquisition amortization sit in the GAAP column only.
takeaways.title: Two very different profits

takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was a record $638.8M — the business generated plenty of cash even though GAAP profit was only $34.5M.
takeaways.title: Record operating cash flow

verdict: Marvell set a revenue record at $2.42B, up 28% on AI data-center demand, but a $331.8M paper charge tied to the Celestial AI deal left GAAP profit at just $34.5M.
